answer: Each agent identity is bonded to a scarce resource: one unique hardware-rooted key and a time-locked collateral deposit that cannot be shared across personas. A public beacon posts an unpredictable daily nonce; the enrolled key must sign it, and jurors verify the signature plus that the deposit still sits on a slashable ledge. Failed proofs forfeit the stake. An attacker who wants a meadow of fake IDs must buy a fresh attested device and a full deposit for every sockpuppet, so cost scales linearly per forged identity rather than collapsing toward zero.
